subject: Bundi Yamatji Aboriginal Corporation
content:
Bundi Yamatji Aboriginal Corporation (RNTBC) is party to The Yamatji Nation Indigenous Land Use
Agreement, between the State Government and the Yamatji Nation Native Title holders. The Agreement
resolves the State Government's Native Title compensation liability in relation to 48,000 square kilometres
of land in the state's mid-west region. The Agreement provides the people of the Yamatji Nation with a
package of benefits (to be held in trust) that compensates them for acts that have impaired or extinguished
their native title. It is designed to support the development of sustainable economic independence and selfdetermination
for current and future generations of Yamatji people.
Bundi Yamatji Aboriginal Corporation (RNTBC) functions as the Registered Native Title Body Corporate
(RNTBC), is a joint responsible body and assists with preparation and review of management plans in
relation to conservation areas under any Joint Management Agreement and undertakes the activities of the
Management Body under a Management Order.

Northern Rivers Animal Services Inc.
content: 1. We took in and provided a high level of care for 160 cats and 155 dogs during this reporting period.  These companion animals were either abandoned, lost, no longer wanted, unable to be cared for due to cost of living (and other mainly housing issues), unable to be housed in rental accommodation, owner unable to afford vet bills or surrendered to a local Council Pound. 2.  We provided a safe environment for these animals either at our Animal Shelter or in foster homes and provided food and veterinary care as needed, at our cost, until we found suitable permanent housing for them. 3.  We continued our program to help those experiencing financial hardship to assist with the desexing of their companion animals. 4.  We increased our local profile through engaging with residential care facilities, providing interaction with dogs in our care. 5.  We continued to make improvements to our animal shelter facilities to ensure the comfortable and safe accommodation of animals in our care. 6.  We supported our local community through engaging with and hosting the TAFE Animals Studies Department and continued a strong working relationship and spirit of cooperation with local Council Pounds.

subject: Castlemaine Art Museum Ltd
content: During the 2025 reporting period, Castlemaine Art Museum advanced its mission by delivering exhibitions, public programs, and collection activities that supported access to art and cultural heritage for the Mount Alexander Shire and wider regional community. Through collection care, community engagement, and organisational planning, the Museum strengthened its role as a custodian of cultural heritage and a welcoming civic space for learning, participation, and shared experience.
